Patients with chronic functional somatic symptoms are experiencing a wide variety of non-cancerous physical complaints that significantly impact their daily lives. These can include persistent pain or discomfort, muscle tension, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and other somatic issues. The diversity of these symptoms means they cannot be classified into well-defined distinct syndromes.

Research suggests that somatic complaints may not only predict but also contribute to the subsequent development of depressive symptoms in women, particularly those with nonclinical populations. However, it is essential to consider social variables and conduct additional research to better understand predictors of depressive symptoms in men.

The overall increase in Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) use among U.S. adults with chronic disease-related functional limitations from 2002 to 2007 highlights the growing interest in these therapies. Despite this, reports of mechanical dysfunction in chronic oro-facial pain are not necessarily related to somatization, as psychological factors also play a role.

Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is often diagnosed as a diagnosis of exclusion due to its high comorbidity with other functional gastrointestinal disorders and the lack of clear diagnostic criteria. However, expert opinions may vary on whether IBS should be classified as such. More stringent guidelines for diagnosis could improve consistency in care.

Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) has been used to predict recovery in patients with disorders of consciousness by identifying areas of brain activity associated with improvement. This method holds promise but requires further evaluation to achieve accurate predictions and minimize variation in patient outcomes.

Body dysmorphic disorder may have a psychotic subtype that overlaps or is the same as somatic type delusional disorder, suggesting its consideration for inclusion in future editions of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM).

Reducing spasticity can improve arm function in patients with arm spasm. A targeted meta-analytic approach can demonstrate this association.

Multi-modal cervical physical therapy has shown a positive effect on subjective tinnitus complaints in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus, although larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and explore the potential role of fenofibrate in sleep apnea syndrome.
